comments.author: cosmotic
comments.story: Oracle Will Not Voluntarily Withdraw JavaScript Trademark
comments.why: Explains trademark defense from Velcro's perspective
comments.text: JavaScript can refer to many different similar languages, the runtimes, the standard library, etc. People using JavaScript without getting permission are potentially infringing on Oracle's trademark. Many companies with trademarks tenaciously defend the trademark to protect it from being revoked. This doesn't appear to be the case with JavaScript. After usage becomes widespread, a company risks losing their trademark because they did not actively enforce the use of the trademark. This video explains it from Velcro's perspective [VIDEO]

comments.author: SushiHippie
comments.story: List of Generic and Genericized Trademarks
comments.why: Velcro ad as example of defending a trademark.
comments.text: After reading the post about Super Bowl [0] I remembered the Velcro advertisement [1] and wondered what else are genericized trademarks. I think everyone is aware that Velcro, Kleenex, post-it are trademarks, even though they are used for off-brand products colloquially. In Germany people also use Tempo, Tesa, Edding and so on, but most are aware that these are brand names. But I was surprised to find out that names like escalator, cellophane, flip phone, even dry ice, trampoline, dumpster were once brand names!
